cases.purpose: mkfs on a loop block device takes the size from BLKGETSIZE64 (4 MiB -> 4096 1 KiB blocks, then 1024 4 KiB blocks), writes the label and reserved percentage, and the result passes e2fsck -fn and mounts and stores data.
cases.oracle: blockdev --getsize64, dumpe2fs -h and e2fsck -fn from e2fsprogs read the device independently; reserved blocks = floor(blocks*10/100) as mke2fs computes.
cases.comparison: Candidate output, status and files compared with values derived independently of candidate output.
cases.script:
. ./rl.sh
/usr/bin/truncate -s 4M m.img
at m.img; L=$REPLY
dump() { /usr/sbin/dumpe2fs -h $L 2>/dev/null; }
field() { local k=$1 l; v=; while IFS= read -r l; do [[ $l == "$k:"* ]] && { v=${l#*:}; v=${v#"${v%%[![:space:]]*}"}; return; }; done < <(dump); }
mkfs -L BLKDEV $L >o.txt 2>e.txt; rc=$?
echo "mkfs status=$rc device-bytes=$(/usr/sbin/blockdev --getsize64 $L)"
field "Block count"; b=$v; field "Block size"; s=$v; field "Filesystem volume name"; n=$v
echo "fs: blocks=$b bsize=$s label=$n"
/usr/sbin/e2fsck -fn $L >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "e2fsck=$?"
/usr/bin/mkdir -p mnt; /usr/bin/mount $L mnt; echo "mount status=$?"
echo hi > mnt/f; read -r d < mnt/f; echo "data=$d"; /usr/bin/umount mnt
mkfs -F -b 4096 -m 10 -L BLK4K $L >o.txt 2>e.txt; echo "second status=$?"
field "Block count"; b=$v; field "Block size"; s=$v; field "Filesystem volume name"; n=$v; field "Reserved block count"; r=$v
echo "fs: blocks=$b bsize=$s label=$n reserved=$r"
/usr/sbin/e2fsck -fn $L >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "e2fsck=$?"
cases.stdout:
mkfs status=0 device-bytes=4194304
fs: blocks=4096 bsize=1024 label=BLKDEV
e2fsck=0
mount status=0
data=hi
second status=0
fs: blocks=1024 bsize=4096 label=BLK4K reserved=102
e2fsck=0
